properties.name: Curia Iulia
properties.description: Construction of the Curia Julia was begun by Julius Caesar and completed by Augustus in 29 BCE. It replaced the former senate house, the Curia Hostilia.

properties.name: Divorum
properties.description: A porticus constructed by Domitian in A.D. 80 on the eastern Campus Martius on the site of the Villa Publica, whose northern entry—a triumphal arch—was flanked by two small temples in honor of Titus and Vespasian.

properties.name: Domus Flavia

properties.name: Domus Romane di Palazzo Valentini
properties.description: The remains of a Roman domus and a bath complex adjacent to the area of the Forum of Trajan.

properties.name: Domus di Vigna Guidi

properties.name: Excubitorium
properties.description: A barracks of the seventh cohort of the Vigiles, Rome's urban fire brigade, was located in the Transtiberim.

properties.name: Forum Augusti
properties.description: The Forum of Augustus at Rome was dedicated in 2 BCE, to the northeast of Julius Caesar's Forum. It contained the Temple of Mars Ultor.

properties.name: Forum of Nerva
properties.description: A forum complex at Rome begun under Domitian but completed under Nerva and dedicated in A.D. 97. Sometimes referred to as the Forum Transitorium, the complex was the next to last of the imperial fora at Rome.

properties.name: Funerary Chamber of Manlia Felicitas
properties.description: A subterranean funerary chamber with three frescoes walls depicting animal and vegetal life, located around the third mile of the Via Appia.

properties.name: Giordani
properties.description: A fourth-century A.D. catacomb along the via Salaria at Rome.

properties.name: Horologium Augusti

properties.name: Horrea Agrippiana
properties.description: A set of warehouses in Regio VIII.

properties.name: Horrea Piperataria

properties.name: Horrea Vespasiani
properties.description: A warehouse complex on the Palatine slope adjacent to the Sacra Via.

properties.name: Horti Lucull(i)ani
properties.description: An elite villa and garden on the Pincian Hill in Rome laid out originally by Lucius Licinius Lucullus ca. 60 BC. The present day Villa Borghese gardens still cover a portion of the Gardens of Lucullus.

properties.description: A Roman hypogeum-type tomb in the via Teodora was reused in the construction of the tower known as Torre del Giudizio.

properties.name: Hypogeum of Trebius Giustus
properties.description: A tomb of the fourth century A.D. located on the Via Latina.

properties.name: Hypogeum of the Aurelii
properties.description: A third-century AD hypogeum tomb on the Esquiline Hill in Rome with both pagan and Paleochristian iconography.

properties.description: A circular mausoleum dating to the Late Republican period along the Via Praenestina.

properties.name: Largo Preneste
properties.description: A Roman tomb of the second or third century CE.

properties.name: Le Vignacce
properties.description: A Roman villa located on via Lemonia in Rome's suburbium attributed to Quintus Servilius Pudens.

properties.name: Lucio Vero
properties.description: A Roman villa located at Acquatraversa on the Via Cassia that is frequently attributed to Lucius Verus.

properties.name: Lucus Stimulae
properties.description: A grove sacred to Stimula, located at the southwestern foot of the Aventine Hill.

properties.name: Ludus Magnus
properties.description: A gladiatorial training school adjacent to the Flavian Amphitheater in Rome. The structure is attested on the Severan marble plan of Rome.

properties.name: Marmenia

properties.name: Mars, Aedes

properties.name: Mausoleum of Lucilius Peto
properties.description: A tumulus-type tomb discovered in 1887 belonging to the military tribune M. Lucilius Paetus of the gens Lucilia.

properties.name: Mausoleum of Menenius Agrippa
properties.description: The so-called mausoleum of Menenius Agrippa stands along the Via Nomentana.

properties.name: Mausoleum of Tor di Quinto

properties.name: Monte Testaccio
properties.description: An artificial mountain on the banks of the Tiber River at Rome composed of 580,000 cubic meters of broken amphorae.

properties.name: Monte del Grano
properties.description: Monte del Grano is a popular name that was assigned to a mausoleum once thought to belong to Alexander Severus, although that assignation is no longer supported. The archaeological remains are now part of the Parco XVII…

properties.name: Murus Romuli
properties.description: "Murus Romuli" refers to a fortification wall alleged to have surrounded the Palatine Hill in Rome, Italy. Legendary tradition claims it was built by the founder-hero Romulus during the eighth century BCE. The…

properties.name: Murus Terreus Carinarum
properties.description: An early earthwork at Rome described by Varro, the Murus Terreus may have been part of the so-called Servian Wall. It was likely located on the Oppian Hill, between the Subura and the Carinae.

properties.name: Naumachia
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Naumachia

properties.name: Ninfeo della Lucchina
properties.description: A nymphaeum of the third century CE that was identified in 1990 and was likely one component of a larger villa complex in the north-west suburbium of imperial Rome.

properties.name: Nymphaeum divi Alexandri
properties.description: A monumental nymphaeum on the Esquiline Hill dating to the Severan period; commonly known as "Trofei di Mario". The complex is located at a fork between the Via Tiburtina and the Via Labicana.

properties.name: Nymphaeum of Egeria
properties.description: A nymphaeum connected with Egeria, the divine advisor of Numa Pompilius. This iteration of Egeria's spring dates to the time of Herodes Atticus in the second century A.D.

properties.name: Octagonal hall, Villa dei Gordiani
properties.description: A Roman structure with three levels that was re-purposed in the Middle Ages, the so-called Octagonal hall at the Villa dei Gordiani was likely originally either a nymphaeum or part of a bath complex.

properties.name: Ospedale di S. Camillo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Ospedale di S. Camillo

properties.name: Osteria di Centocelle
properties.description: An nymphaeum located at Osteria di Centocelle dating to the Roman Imperial period.

properties.name: Paedagogium

properties.description: "Palatine Stadium" is likely a misnomer when considering the probable function of this architectural complex located on the southeast corner of the Palatine Hill on the flank of the Domus Augustana-Flavia. Originating…

properties.name: Palatium Sessorianum
properties.description: Palatium Sessorianum is of unknown origins. It was situated at the extreme south-east of Region V and it adjoined the amphitheatrum Castrense. It pre-dated the Aurelian wall. The portions of the complex within the line…

properties.name: Parco delle Tombe di via Latina
properties.description: A cluster of Roman Imperial tombs along the Via Latina excavated in the nineteenth century.

properties.name: Piazza Ronchi Roman cistern
properties.description: A Roman cistern dating to the second-third centuries CE.

properties.name: Pons Aelius
properties.description: The Pons Aelius or Aelian Bridge (now Ponte Sant'Angelo) was completed by Hadrian in AD 134 to span the Tiber opposite the new mausoleum of the emperor.

properties.name: Pons Neronianus
properties.description: A bridge across the Tiber river built either by Caius or Nero in order to connect the western part of the Campus Martius with the Campus Vaticanus.

properties.name: Ponte Nomentano
properties.description: A Roman bridge over the Aniene river.

properties.name: Ponte Romano di Parco dei Medici
properties.description: The ruins of a second-century A.D. Roman bridge at Magliana Vecchia.

properties.name: Porta Appia
properties.description: A gate in the Aurelian Wall through which the Via Appia passed. Now known as Porta S. Sebastiano.

properties.name: Porta Ardeatina

properties.name: Porta Aurelia
properties.description: A gate in the Aurelian Wall at the summit of the Ianiculum through which the Via Aurelia passes.

properties.name: Porta Flumentana

properties.name: Porta Maggiore
properties.description: The Porta Maggiore is the ancient Porta Praenestina, an early Imperial gate preserved in the later third century walls built by Aurelian.

properties.name: Porta Mugonia
properties.description: The Porta Mugonia was one of the three gates of the original Palatine city of Rome (often referred to as "Roma quadrata"). Its precise location can no longer be established and it remains a hotly debated issue for…

properties.name: Porta Naevia
properties.description: The now-lost Porta Naevia was a minor gate in the Republican-period wall of the city of Rome. It was located on the Little Aventine and its position may correspond to the modern Largo Enzo Fioritto.

properties.name: Porta Ostiensis
properties.description: The Porta Ostiensis, now known as the Porta San Paolo, is a gate in Rome's Aurelian Wall from which the Via Ostiensis issues.

properties.name: Porta Querquetulana
properties.description: The Porta Querquetulana was a gateway of Rome's so-called Servian Walls. It derived its name from from a sacred grove of oaks that seems to have vanished by the first century BCE.

properties.name: Porta Rauduscula
properties.description: The Porta Rauduscula was a gate of Rome's so-called Servian Wall. It is known only from textual sources. Varro's listing places it between the Porta Naevia and the Porta Lavernalis.

properties.name: Porticus Boni Eventus
properties.description: A portico built in 374 CE by an urban prefect named Claudius near the temple of the god Bonus Eventus.

properties.name: Pozzo Pantaleo
properties.description: The 'Pozzo Pantaleo' is a Roman mausoleum that re-used a cistern of the early Imperial period. In a third phase, the site was repurposed as a shrine dedicated to the Christian Saint Pantaleon.

properties.name: Praedia Galbana
properties.description: A tract of suburban land located southwest of the Aventine Hill that would come to be the location of the Horrea Galbae.

properties.name: Priscilla

properties.name: Pyramidal tomb of the Via Appia
properties.description: A pyramid-shaped Roman tomb located along the Appian Way that may have belonged to the family of the Quintilii.

properties.name: Quadraro

properties.name: Quintilii
properties.description: A suburban villa built by Sextus Quintilius Maximus and Sextus Quintilius Condianus (consuls in A.D. 151).

properties.name: Redicolo
properties.description: The Tomb of Annia Regilla (vix. A.D. 125-160), the wife of Herodes Atticus. The tomb is also erroneously known as the "Temple of the God Rediculum" and was used in the Middle Ages as a hay barn.

properties.name: Regia

properties.name: Roman Mausoleum of Villa Gordiani

properties.name: Roman cistern
properties.description: A Roman cistern at the Villa Gordiani.

properties.name: Roman cistern
properties.description: A Roman cistern of the early second century A.D.

properties.name: Roman villa at Anagnina Metro station
properties.description: The archaeological remains of a villa in the suburbium of the city of Rome located adjacent to what is now a station of the Rome Metro system at Anagnina.

properties.name: Rostra
properties.description: A large platform erected in the Forum Romanum for senators to deliver orations to a crowd.

properties.name: S. Agnese

properties.name: S. Alessandro
properties.description: The basilica and catacombs of S. Alessandro are located at the seventh milestone of the Via Nomentana.

properties.name: S. Callisto
properties.description: A large catacomb on the Via Appia south of Rome notable especially for its so-called 'Crypt of the Popes'. The catacomb covers approximately 15 hectares.

properties.name: S. Cesareo
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 S. Cesareo

properties.name: S. Ermete
properties.description: S. Ermete is the site of a Paleochristian basilica and catacomb; the catacombs are also referred to as the Catacombs of Bassilla, and both names occur in the documentary sources.

properties.name: S. Felicita
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 S. Felicita

properties.name: S. Ippolito
properties.description: A catacomb connected with the Christian Saint Hippolytus of Rome along the Via Tiburtina.

properties.name: S. Laurentius

properties.name: S. Passera

properties.name: S. Passera hypogeum
properties.description: A hypogeum connected with the S. Passera complex.

properties.name: S. Paulus
properties.description: One of Rome's four major papal basilicae, S. Paulus was founded by Constantine I in the early fourth century A.D. and expanded by Valentinian I in the 370s. The basilica, with many renovations, repairs, and…

properties.name: S. Petrus

properties.name: S. Sebastianus
properties.description: S. Sebastianus (San Sebastiano fuori le mura) is a Christian basilica outside the walls of Rome; the earliest phase belongs to the fourth century AD.

properties.name: S. Valentino
properties.description: A Christian catacomb along the Via Flaminia dedicated to S. Valentino.

properties.name: Saepta Iulia
properties.description: An enclosure in the Campus Martius surrounded by porticoes built by Marcus Agrippa before ca. 26 BCE.

properties.name: Schola Praeconum

properties.name: Sep. Bibuli
properties.description: The tomb of C. Publicius Bibulus, a plebeian aedile, located at Rome at the foot of the Capitoline Hill. It most likely dates to the close of the Republican period.

properties.name: Sep. Eurysacis
properties.description: The tomb of a baker, M. Vergilius Eurysaces, built at the point where the via Labicana and the via Praenestina exit from Rome's walls to the east. The tomb dates to the later Republican period (ca. 50-20 B.C.).

properties.name: Sep. Geta
properties.description: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that is traditionally believed to be that of Publius Septimius Geta, the younger son of Septimius Severus.

properties.name: Sepolcreto Ostiense

properties.name: Sepolcro dei Calpurni
properties.description: Sepolcro dei Calpurni is a Roman hypogeum tomb along the Via Latina that dates to the middle of the first century CE.

properties.name: Septizonium

properties.name: Sette Sale
properties.description: Cisterns of the imperial period on the Oppian Hill that once supplied the Baths of Trajan.

properties.name: Shrine of Strenia
properties.description: The Shrine of Strenia was located in the valley of the Colosseum and is mentioned as the starting point of the Sacra Via.

properties.name: So-called Arco di Druso

properties.name: So-called Tempio di Venere e Cupido

properties.name: Subura

properties.name: Temple of Divus Augustus (Rome)

properties.name: Temple of Divus Iulius
properties.description: The temple on the Sacra Via dedicated to the deified Iulius Caesar, authorized in 42 B.C. and built by Augustus, with its dedication occurring on 18th August, 29 B.C.

properties.name: Temple of Jupiter?, Via Appia
properties.description: A temple located at the fourth mile of the Via Appia.

properties.name: Temple of Mars Ultor
properties.description: The Temple of Mars Ultor was dedicated in the Forum of Augustus in 2 B.C., fulfilling a vow that Octavian had made to the god in 42 B.C.

properties.name: Temple of Minerva Medica
properties.description: The so-called Temple of Minerva Medica is, in fact, a nymphaeum located along the line of the Anio Vetus aqueduct; it most likely dates to the fourth century AD.

properties.name: Templum Pacis
properties.description: The Temple of Peace in Rome was vowed by Vespasian following the Jewish War.

properties.name: Templum Veneris et Romae
properties.description: A double temple sacred to Venus Felix and Roma Aeterna built by Hadrian on the slope of the Velian hill to the north of the Sacra Via beginning in 121 CE.

properties.name: Theatrum Marcelli
properties.description: Theatrum Marcelli (Theater of Marcellus) is an ancient Roman theater in the Circus Flaminius. Augustus completed its construction and dedicated it in 12 BC.

properties.name: Thermae Antoninianae
properties.description: The Thermae Antoninianae, commonly known as the Baths of Caracalla, were built in Rome between AD 212 and 216.

properties.name: Thermae Diocletiani
properties.description: Public baths near the Viminal Hill in Rome constructed under Diocletian from 298-306 CE.

properties.name: Thermae Helenianae

properties.name: Thermae Traiani
properties.description: A monumental public bath of ancient Rome that was built between 104 and 109. The architect Apollodorus of Damascus built the baths for Trajan.

properties.name: Tomb Garden of Claudia Semne
properties.description: Latin inscriptions unearthed in 1792 between the second and third mile of the Via Appia near S. Sebastiano identify the tomb garden complex of one Claudia Semne.

properties.name: Tomb of Gaius Rabirius Postumus Libertus and family
properties.description: A tomb of the Republican period belonging to the freedman family of the Rabirii.

properties.name: Tomb of Hilarus Fuscus
properties.description: The Late Republican tomb of the freedman Hilarus Fuscus along the Via Appia (ca. 30 B.C.).

properties.name: Tomb of Marcus Servilius Quartus
properties.description: A Roman tomb on the Via Appia dating ca. A.D. 100.

properties.name: Tomb of Priscilla
properties.description: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia that belonged to one Priscilla, wife of Titus Flavius Abascanto, a freedman of the emperor Domitian.

properties.name: Tomb of Septimia Galla
properties.description: A Roman tomb at the sixth mile of the Via Appia.

properties.name: Tomb of Tiberius Claudius Secundus
properties.description: A Roman tomb along the Via Appia.

properties.name: Tomb of Vibius Marianus
properties.description: An imperial Roman tomb of Publius Vibius Marianus, erroneously identified as the Tomba di Nerone (Tomb of Nero) by G. B. Piranesi.

properties.name: Tomb of the Nasonii
properties.description: The tomb of the Nasonii family is an ancient Roman hypogeum-type tomb along the Via Flaminia in Grottarossa in the northern outskirts of Rome. The tomb was exposed during road works in 1674.

properties.name: Tomb of the Ottavii

properties.name: Tomb of the Servilii
properties.description: A tomb known as the "Tomb of the Servilii" which pre-dates the Mausoleum of Romulus, was incorporated into the porticus surrounding the latter. This tomb dates to the late first century BCE or early first century CE.

properties.name: Tomba della Medusa (Roma)
properties.description: A Roman chamber tomb now located on the grounds of the Policlinico Umberto I hospital in Rome.

properties.name: Tomba della Vaschetta
properties.description: The so-called "Tomba della Vaschetta" is a Roman tomb located in the Portuense necropolis.

properties.name: Tomba di Fadilla
properties.description: A Roman tomb on the Via Flaminia at Grottarossa that is associated with Annia Aurelia Fadilla, the daughter of the emperor Marcus Aurelius.

properties.name: Tor Marancia
properties.description: The modern toponym Tor Marancia is claimed to derive from the Praedium Amaranthianus, a villa belonging to the second-century A.D. freedman Amaranthus.

properties.name: Torre Dell'Angelo
properties.description: A Roman columbarium tomb located on the Via Latina.

properties.name: Unnamed bridge
properties.description: A Roman bridge located in the Parco dei Medici near Rome, Italy.

properties.name: Unnamed bridge (Cessati Spiriti)
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 C2 unnamed bridge (Cessati Spiriti)

properties.name: Via Berneri columbarium
properties.description: The Via Berneri columbarium was discovered in 2021 during utility work. This Roman tomb contained two sarcophagi, one of which carried a Latin inscription.

properties.name: Via Olevano Romano columbarium
properties.description: A late republican to early imperial columbarium along the Via Praenestina. The columbarium is of rectangular plan and was last used during the early Flavian period.

properties.name: Via Pollenza Roman villa
properties.description: A Roman villa complex that was occupied beginning in the first century BCE.

properties.name: Via Taranto columbaria
properties.description: Two early imperial columbaria were discovered in 1932 along the Via Taranto.

properties.name: Via Triumphalis necropolis
properties.description: A segment of an imperial necropolis preserved along a portion of a consular road on the Vatican Hill. The Via Triumphalis necropolis was uncovered during the construction of a parking structure in the Via del Pellegrino.

properties.name: Vicus Censorius
properties.description: A street located on the Tiber Island that connected the Pons Cestius and Pons Fabricius. It is cited on the so-called "Capitoline Base".

properties.name: Vicus Drusianus
properties.description: A street located in Regio I of ancient Rome that is known from the so-called Capitoline Base (CIL 6, 975). Part of its course may correspond to the Via della Ferratella in Laterano.

properties.name: Vigna Pia necropolis
properties.description: An imperial necropolis with columbarium tombs and a family tomb connected with the gens Atilia Romana.

properties.name: Vigna Randanini
properties.description: A Jewish catacomb along the Via Appia discovered in 1859.

properties.name: Villa Collatino
properties.description: Remains of a Roman villa discovered in the Collatino archaeological park in Via Grotta di Gregna consisting of 14 rooms, a cistern, and channelization for water works.

properties.name: Villa Esmeade
properties.description: An ancient place, cited: BAtlas 43 B2 Villa Esmeade

properties.name: Villa Pamphili

properties.name: Villa Torlonia
properties.description: A Jewish catacomb discovered in 1919 on the grounds of the Villa Torlonia park in Rome.

properties.name: Villa di Faonte a Vigne Nuove
